checks.name: name-matches-directory
checks.rule: `name:` field matches the skill's directory name

checks.name: trigger-phrases
checks.rule: Description includes at least 2 explicit trigger phrases

specificity.reasoning: Very precise: mentions create/read/edit/manipulate, specific formatting features (TOC, headings, page numbers, letterheads), tracked changes, comments, find-and-replace, images

triggerCoverage.reasoning: Comprehensive triggers: Word doc, word document, .docx, report/memo/letter/template, plus action verbs for extraction, reorganization, images, tracked changes

boundaryclarity.reasoning: Explicit negative triggers: Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation

distinctiveness.reasoning: Clearly distinct from pdf/pptx/xlsx by file type (.docx) and use case (Word documents). No meaningful overlap with other skills

descriptionJudge.summary: Excellent description with precise capabilities, comprehensive trigger phrases covering file types and natural language terms, explicit exclusions, and clear distinctiveness from sibling document skills.

actionability.reasoning: Every instruction is concrete with exact code examples, bash commands, and critical rules clearly marked. Quick reference table maps tasks to approaches immediately.

completeness.reasoning: Covers creation (docx-js), editing (unpack/XML/repack), reading (pandoc), conversion (.doc to .docx, to images), tracked changes, comments, images, XML reference, validation, and auto-repair. Error handling via validate.py.

codeQuality.reasoning: Excellent runnable JavaScript and bash code with critical warnings (e.g., never use unicode bullets, always set page size, tables need dual widths). Common pitfalls well documented.

conciseness.reasoning: At 19K chars it is lengthy, but the complexity of the OOXML format and the number of gotchas (docx-js quirks, XML schema compliance, tracked changes patterns) justifies most of the content. Some redundancy in critical rules section vs inline warnings.

contentJudge.summary: Highly actionable and comprehensive skill covering all major docx workflows with excellent code quality. Slightly verbose due to the inherent complexity of the format, but nearly all content is justified.
